claims.text: A three-server MCP setup (GitHub, Playwright, IDE) consumed 143,000 of a 200,000-token context window (72%) with tool definitions before reading a user message.
GitHub Copilot cut its tool count from 40 to 13, gaining a 400-millisecond latency reduction and a 2 to 5 percentage point accuracy improvement.
Dynamic progressive tool loading in MCP cuts schema tokens to under 2.5K from 410K.
MCP tool definitions consume 200-500 tokens per tool on average, and GitHub's official MCP server alone consumes roughly 26,000 to 55,000 tokens depending on the measurement source.
Claude Desktop performance degrades at 30-50 active tool schemas, and industry consensus puts a practical ceiling at 5 to 7 connected MCP servers.
Block's Finance Copilot, built on MCP, answered 40 leadership questions, cutting time from 7.6 hours to under 1 hour with 100% accuracy on governed metrics.
Block's internal "Block Data MCP" workflow reached 1,812 quarterly unique users in Q1 2026.
Eon uses A2A 0.3 for a multi-agent assistant over business data, with 3 remote specialists and about 20 function calls, enabling independent deploys and tenant additions without code changes.
Huawei uses A2A in production for its HarmonyOS assistant to hand tasks to in-app agents.
Elastic demonstrates a hybrid pattern in which a Reporter Agent delegates research via A2A and an Archive Agent uses MCP to access Elasticsearch tools.
MCP authorization in 2026 requires servers to implement OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) and clients to implement Resource Indicators (RFC 8707) to bind tokens to specific servers.
For MCP, gateways mint and bind credentials, whereas for A2A, gateways only validate credentials that agents already carry.
A2A requires clients to authenticate with a scheme declared in the Agent Card but does not decide which callers may invoke which agent; authorization is separate.
Astrix's analysis found 53% of 5,200 MCP servers rely on insecure long-lived static secrets, while only 8.5% use OAuth.

By early 2026 about 7,000 internet-exposed MCP servers existed, roughly 50% without authentication controls; a July 2025 scan found 1,862 publicly accessible MCP servers responding to unauthenticated requests.
CVE-2025-6514 was an unauthenticated RCE in Anthropic's MCP Inspector, caused by failure to sanitize the authorization_endpoint URL.
A peer-reviewed study found MCP attack success rates from 0% in Claude Desktop (which sandboxes tools) to 100% in Cursor (which auto-executes tool calls without confirmation).
The MCPTox benchmark showed that malicious instructions embedded in tool descriptions can manipulate agent behavior with high success rates across 45 real-world MCP servers.
2025 incidents included cross-tenant data exposure at Asana from an access control misconfiguration, and prompt injection against a GitHub MCP server via an overly broad personal access token.

AWS AgentCore Gateway (GA Mar 3, 2026) uses Cedar policies with default-deny, intercepts all tools/list and tools/call requests, omits denied actions from tool lists, and supports Lambda interceptors that check DynamoDB allowed tools and filter sensitive information by user permissions.

Google Agent Registry requires manual registration of external MCP servers with a toolspec.json file (max 10 KB), and IAM Unified Access Policies authorize each tool at execution time outside the model reasoning loop; the Gateway uses IAP CEL policies to block destructive tools and unregistered URLs.

Microsoft Foundry Toolbox aggregates MCP servers into one endpoint and enforces allowed_tools and require_approval policies at the runtime layer, because the MCP endpoint itself does not block tools/call; it also applies RAI guardrails to screen tool inputs and outputs for prompt injection.

Production gateway validation pipelines check server trust, tool eligibility (RBAC/ABAC), schema shape, sanitization of instruction-like patterns, and runtime re-validation; tool list pinning prevents servers from changing tool definitions mid-conversation.
Most production teams converge on an allowlist model where new MCP servers enter the registry only after review.
